data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is primarily an anthropogenic heat effect: human combustion and building HVAC emissions directly warm the urban air after sunset, and the gap scales with population density and city size.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a city has low energy consumption or mild climate requiring minimal HVAC, anthropogenic heat is insufficient to explain the gap.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If wind speed is high, anthropogenic heat is dispersed and cannot sustain a localized UHI.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the observed UHI persists in the absence of measurable anthropogenic flux, other mechanisms must dominate.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Waste heat from transportation, industry, and space heating is released directly into the urban atmosphere; on calm nights this heat is not advected away and accumulates in the shallow urban boundary layer; larger, denser cities with greater energy consumption exhibit a stronger nocturnal UHI.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
